record.notes: Storage is generous and compute is not. 100 projects x 1 GB is 100 GB nominal, but each project also gets 100 CU-hours, so the shape is 100 small workloads and not one 100 GB database. The free tier does not delete data; it suspends compute or blocks writes. The measured 100 MB cap belongs to the anonymous Claimable path, not the free plan, and conflating them is the easy error. The vector extension was installed and queried, not merely listed as available, so `pgvector on a free Postgres` is a working chain and not an inference.

egress.terms: 5 GB/month public network transfer per project, shared across Postgres, object storage and functions; then $0.10/GB on paid only. Free is a hard 5 GB.

record.tooling: Real S3 API (`forcePathStyle: true`, path-style only), AWS SDK/boto3/aws CLI, `neon buckets` CLI, files-sdk.dev `neon` adapter. Endpoint is per-branch: https://br-<name>.storage.<cell>.<region>.aws.neon.tech
record.chaining: 100 projects/org (Free) x 5 GB object storage = 500 GB; x 20 GB Postgres cap = only 20 GB of DB storage, but object storage is NOT under that 20 GB cap. It is per project. Add branches: 10 branches/project, objects branch without copying. Multiple orgs per account are allowed ('one Neon account can belong to multiple orgs on different plans').
record.limits_note: Max object size 5 GiB; throttling returns 503 SlowDown under load; path-style only, no virtual-host buckets; ACL/policy must be set via Console/API, not S3 wire. 5 GB egress/project/month is the real wall for serving.
record.reliability_note: Compute scale-to-zero after 5 min (Free, cannot disable); project data persists. Rate limiting is documented and retryable.
